name: Ives (The Ives, phase one)
headline: Foothills Regional Housing (the Jefferson County Housing Authority) built The Ives, 50 one-bedroom apartments at 4470 Wadsworth Blvd. in Wheat Ridge with 25 project-based-voucher units for people leaving homelessness and 24 units at 60% AMI, using $1,210,000 a year in 2022 federal 9% credits; it opened in June 2024.
why_it_matters: It is the first phase of a housing-authority campus on land the authority already owned, and it set up Ives II (98 units, 2025 awards) next door with city-donated land and city-assigned bond cap.

status.label: Built and occupied (opened June 2024)
status.detail: Ground was broken on April 25 (2023, inferred from a December 2023 article describing work under way); Foothills Regional Housing says it opened the doors in June 2024 and the property is occupied. Foothills lists it as completed in 2024. No 8609 or placed-in-service record was found.

next_step: Confirm the 8609 year and final credit in CHFA or HUD placed-in-service data; follow Ives II (ives-ii-wheat-ridge.json) for the next phase.

background.text: Land: the housing authority already owned the site (with a garage built in 2011) and also owns the adjacent former Pep Boys, O'Reilly Auto Parts and Bank of the West properties, where it plans further phases.
The 25 homeless units are a preference rather than a hard set-aside: they can be leased to other qualified low-income tenants if no referral is available.

Neighbors said at an October 2023 meeting they had not been told before work started; the housing authority said it met all city notice requirements because the site was already zoned for multifamily.

For phase two, the City of Wheat Ridge assigned more than $1.9M of its private activity bond cap to Foothills and, on 2023-09-25, rezoned the city-owned former Bank of the West parcel so it could be sold to Foothills for $10.
The Wadsworth Boulevard widening ('Improve Wadsworth', about $70M) began in October 2021 alongside the site.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award description gives 15 units at 30% AMI, 10 at 50% and 24 at 60% plus one employee unit, while a 2025 trade association summary says 25 units are at 30% to 50% AMI and the remaining 25 at 60%.

The application planned up to $500,000 of Jefferson County HOME or CDBG money and $55,000 per unit from DOH, while 2023 reporting gives $1 million of county federal funds and $3.25 million from the Department of Local Affairs.
